title: Build a structured-output AI feature
summary: Turn short notes into useful records, and learn why valid JSON can still be wrong.
outcome: A note-to-records application, error cases and an evaluation report.
prerequisites: Run a Python script and explain a dictionary.
Use the JSON, testing and API refreshers if these are unfamiliar.
teaching_question: When does a valid record still misrepresent a note?

lessons.title: Define what a useful record means
lessons.objective: Specify a task record without guessing missing information.
lessons.explanation: Start with examples you own: a clear task, an ambiguous request and a note containing no task. Separate required content from nullable information. A schema constrains structure; it cannot establish whether the note supports a field.
lessons.example:
record = {"task": "Review the deployment guide", "owner": None,
          "source": "Please review the deployment guide."}
assert record["owner"] is None
# An absent owner stays unknown; a note without a task yields no record.
lessons.exercise: Write six notes and their expected records first. Define the schema, including what happens when no task is present. Implement the contract using Pydantic or a small explicit validator.
lessons.completion_check: Valid examples pass; missing required fields and invalid types fail; an absent owner is preserved without invention.
lessons.artifact: A schema, six owned notes and expected records.

lessons.title: Put a model behind a small interface
lessons.objective: Connect extraction to validation through a replaceable adapter.
lessons.explanation: First return a fixed response to test the route from note to record. Then use a separately configured compatible model adapter if one is available. Keep model-generated content as data and record which adapter produced it. Stub results never establish extraction accuracy.
lessons.example:
import json
def parse_response(raw):
    value = json.loads(raw)
    if not isinstance(value, dict):
        raise ValueError("Expected an object")
    return value
assert parse_response('{"owner": null}')["owner"] is None
lessons.exercise: Build a CLI that reads one note and calls the adapter. Validate its response against the previous lesson’s contract. Exercise a fixed valid response, malformed JSON and a timeout.
lessons.completion_check: All three response paths have explicit outcomes. The report identifies whether the transport was stubbed or a model was actually used.
lessons.artifact: A testable CLI and response-adapter contract.

lessons.title: Explain and contain invalid results
lessons.objective: Handle an invalid response without silently fixing its meaning.
lessons.explanation: Keep the original response and a structured error separate from accepted records. A retry can repeat a mistake or spend more resources; set a finite retry policy rather than hiding it inside parsing. Accepting a correction should be a deliberate review step.
lessons.exercise: Add unknown-field, invalid-type, absent-source and timeout cases. Show an actionable error for each. Add a review step before replacing an existing accepted record.
lessons.completion_check: Rejected responses never become accepted records, and repeating a failed call cannot overwrite a previous result.
lessons.artifact: An error table and failure-handling tests.

lessons.title: Measure usefulness on held-out notes
lessons.objective: Distinguish structural validity from supported, useful extraction.
lessons.explanation: Freeze a small held-out note set before changing the prompt. Measure valid-record rate, correctly extracted fields and unsupported fields separately. Keep a development set for iteration so the final check measures unseen cases. Compare against a simple deterministic baseline.
lessons.exercise: Create 20 owned notes, reserving eight for the final check. Record baseline failures, make one change using the other twelve, then evaluate the reserved eight once. Use fixture-only labels if no model ran.
lessons.completion_check: The report includes denominators, unsupported-field examples, a baseline and held-out results under recorded runtime conditions.
lessons.artifact: A runnable evaluation command and a concise failure report.

editorial_status: Draft curriculum; maintainer and learner review pending
assumptions: 10–15 hours weekly is an editable estimate.
Start with standard-library fixtures. Optional libraries and a compatible model runtime need separate setup.
No paid service, model download or hardware capability is assumed.
